comment: I miss the person I was before I took this class. Seriously just don't do it to urself.

There's a midterm and final. Do not take if you aren't interested. He is a harsh grader & feedback makes no sense. Assignments feel like they are graded on vibes rather than guidelines. Participation matters a lot. Only good thing is that there is not a lot of reading. Lectures are boring and very long. He is available outside of class.

Lectures are boring There is a midterm and final. Participation matters a lot. He is accessible outside of class but the assignments are very hard. You have to do scansions that seem to be graded based on vibes and nothing else. There is not a lot of reading (the only good thing about the course). Harsh grader and his feedback makes zero sense.

Professor Schwartz is a great professor but if you aren't interested in poetry like myself you will struggle in this first year seminar unless you want to spend hours and I mean hours on the essays but if you are good at the humanities then you will be fine

Dr. Schwartz is a very knowledgeable and personable guy. His love for poetry is evident and makes it a point to listen to everyone in his class. While the class is almost exclusively lectures with asynchronous reading (which you will then dissect next class in-person), the lectures are decent to very good. The final involves a lot of memorization.

Professor Schwartz is very nice and easy to reach outside of class if you need assistance or have any questions. If you need a gen-ed class for English, I'll recommend him 10/10. Classes are very long and lecture but classwork is very minimal. The class itself exposed me to many poems I never heard of and I'm happy I took his class.
25 years later I still remember him. Truly a wonderful teacher
He is very nice and very knowledgable about his subject matter. The tests are much more difficult than the class, so make sure to study hard for those and take good notes.
Amazing poetry. How could he teach in a so fantasatic way! He is my favorite professor in English department forever

This class helped me learn so much about poetry. You have to know 50 poems for the finals but don't have to memorize them line by line. It's mainly the author's name and the poem's date of publishment. Prof Schwartz will cover the poems enough for you to know what to write about them in the exam so take notes!!

Dr. Schwartz is a really smart professor who makes it clear that he truly enjoys poetry.  FYS Love Poetry was not a lot of work, just a couple of poems to read and analyze each night but the midterm and final are insanely difficult. You need to memorize 30-50 poems which is unrealistic and unnecessary tbh. Helps a lot if you're interested in poetry

I really enjoyed having professor Schwartz for my FYS100 class. We discussed poetry each class with very good detail and I thought that the essays were a good way for us to practice our writing skills. The homework was slight, as it only included poetry annotations before class. Memorizing poems for the midterm and final, however, was unrealistic.

Professor Schwartz is very knowledgeable and his lectures make you think. I've gained a deeper understanding of analyzing poetry and loved many of the poems we read. HOWEVER, HIS TESTS ARE HARD AND UNREASONABLE. his tests require you to study and memorize every poem discussed in class. 50 POEMS!!!! ITS INSANE.
He is really an amazing human being, extremely knowledgable in his area and skillful in teaching.

I really enjoy spending this semester with Prof. Schwartz. Not so much work for most of the semester, but get ready to stay up late before exams. He is incredibly knowledgeable in poetry, knowing every piece and every poet extremely well. Go to his office hour and chat with him! He will give you much more than you thought!

As a student who had complete disinterest in poetry, FYS100 Love Poetry was pleasant due to his enthusiasm. He's a great prof. The workload started off easy (a couple of poems to analyze for homework); however, the midterm and final were unrealistic. Memorizing 30 poems for a midterm and 50 poems for finals isn't useful in my academic career.

Prof Schwartz was a great teacher, he was very passionate and well informed about what he taught. Sometimes class was boring, but he definitely helped me to be more analytical when reading, especially for poetry. Overall great teacher.
Dr. Schwatz will always stand out as one of those truly passionate professors. His class was challenging but he pushes the minds of his students. Definitely an engaging class..TAKE NOTES

For Intro to Poetry, I couldn't have asked for a better professor. He is very invested in his subject, something that a lot of other professors lack. Even though I am an English major, I have found many non-English majors take him for the FSLT requirement. I definitely recommend him highly.
Took Dr. Schwartz for "The Bible as Literature" many moons ago.  Still stands out as one of, if not the most noteworthy class I took at UR.  Highly recommended.

It's easy to tell he really loves what he does. Besides reading and 2 papers there is no homework. Sometimes he starts off the discussion and sometimes he asks the class to start it, which can cause awkward silences. Paper re-writes are great and if you take time to pay attention and discuss in class you'll get a good grade.
He certainly knows a LOT about those books, but sometimes sticks too close to specific questions and class is a little bit too quite. This helps u a lot in understanding those &*&^ books tho.

He loves what he teaches... sometimes when reading he gives out this girlish giggle. If you somewhat read and just pay attetion in class you should have no problem getting a C+ and you get to rewrite all your papers.
Dr. Schwartz always tries to help up understand the material we are presented.  Also, since he has read the core books many times before, he can offer valuable input when analyzing the texts.

Fantastic teacher. Makes any book seem extremely interesting and provokes intelligent and abstract thought with a consistent light-heartedness and humor. If you are willing to engage yourself in the work, you will absolutely be rewarded.
Brilliant professor. Really makes the material fun and exciting. I would definitely recommend this class!

Schwartz is a fantastic lecturer. Class is interesting, informative and entertaining. He's not a push-over, but his grading scheme is fair; it's difficult to receive less than a B/B- on any assignment. Highly recommendeded for everyone, English majors & those looking to fulfill a requirement alike.

One of the best teachers I've had!! He is open to different interpretations as well as explaining his own. He makes any poem interesting and easy to understand. Overall, a great teacher and a great person!!!

Great professor. Really enthusiatic about the material and teaches it well. Very helpful. I wasn't very excited about poetry before I took this class, but he makes it interesting. Fair grading. Little reading. Best class to take to fulfill English requirement.
Incredibly Smart and really nice guy--helpful when you meet with him one on one and very encouraging but very very difficult grader and very hard to grasp material--all core material is boring
Great professor.  Made somewhat antiquated literature fun to read.  Class was challenging and enlightening but not over my head.

He is an awesome professor and it is obvious that he really cares and is interested in his job and in learning in general.  He is willing to help anyone who needs it and explains things until you understand.  He is an awesome professor.

Love this guy, his is extremely intelligent. Very interested in the lit. and the students. Difficult grader but I learned more from him than any other english teacher. he even helped me on other course work as well. He is exciting and excited to teach.Absolutely amazing prof. take him no matter what

Very intelligent. More lecture oriented than most other professors. Wants participation but will flat out say a student is wrong and explain why. Cares about class as shown through his class-specific lesson plans. Not an easy A but anyone taking this class has potential to learn a lot.
